answer: Each identity registers one trellis vine on a ledge terrace, locks a 70-credit bond, and files a sap sample with a Brix reading and serial. A summit auditor recomputes Brix from the public sap table by age, altitude, and week; a reading off by over 2 percent or a reused serial burns the bond. Fees rise per identity: first 34, kth 34+7(k-1), 1000th 7027, so 1000 fakes cost 3,530,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-vine ring fails: one serial seals one sample, and reuse burns both bonds. An honest grower pays 34 once and recovers the bond after a clean audit.
